title: CircleCI Makes Machine Runner Orchestrator Generally Available
gist: CircleCI made Machine Runner Orchestrator 1.0.0 GA, autoscaling self-hosted VM runners across CPU, GPU and ARM from one deployment on GKE, AKS, EKS and KubeVirt at no extra cost; the author frames CI execution capacity as becoming an independently scalable infrastructure layer, competing with GitHub's Actions Runner Controller.

insights.claim: CircleCI's Machine Runner Orchestrator 1.0.0 is GA and autoscales self-hosted machine runner VMs according to CI workload demand, included with self-hosted runners on all plans at no additional cost.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Bundling autoscaling free strengthens CircleCI's self-hosted value proposition against GitHub Actions.
insights.locator: CircleCI has made its Machine Runner

insights.claim: The orchestrator manages CPU, GPU and ARM resource classes from a single deployment, reflecting that CI workloads are no longer homogeneous.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: GPU and ARM CI demand (AI workloads, ARM servers) is rising enough to need unified orchestration.
insights.quote: conventional CPU builds can coexist with GPU-intensive workloads and ARM-based builds without requiring separate orchestration installations for each class
insights.locator: Earlier versions were focused on provisioning

insights.claim: The author argues the real shift is CI execution capacity emerging as an independently scalable infrastructure layer that responds to delivery demand the way platforms already scale application workloads.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Frames CI compute as a distinct elastic infrastructure market for platform engineering spend.
insights.quote: the emergence of CI execution capacity as an independently scalable infrastructure layer

insights.claim: Machine Runner Orchestrator supports GKE, AKS, EKS and KubeVirt, reflecting the increasing use of Kubernetes as the control plane for CI infrastructure while runners themselves stay VM-based.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Reinforces Kubernetes' position as the universal control plane even for non-container workloads.

insights.claim: The orchestrator operates at the CI runner layer, distinct from node autoscalers like Karpenter and Cluster Autoscaler, so both can run together in one architecture.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Positions it as complementary rather than competing with cloud-native autoscaling tooling.
insights.locator: Machine Runner Orchestrator occupies a different layer

insights.claim: GitHub's Actions Runner Controller creates ephemeral Kubernetes-managed runner environments, whereas CircleCI focuses on VM runners, making CircleCI relevant for jobs needing VM-level isolation hard to reproduce in containers.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Defines CircleCI's competitive niche versus GitHub in self-hosted CI.
insights.locator: The difference is largely in the execution

insights.claim: The 1.0 release renames runner-provisioner to machine-runner-orchestrator and cannot be upgraded in place; users must uninstall and reinstall, leaving runners offline during the gap.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Operational friction for existing preview users upgrading production CI.

insights.claim: Version 1.0.0 fixes two high-severity Go gRPC vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-84304 (heap exhaustion via HTTP/2 frame fragmentation) and CVE-2026-84445 (crash on missing :authority/Host header).
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Highlights ongoing HTTP/2 attack surface in widely used gRPC stacks.
